what_it_does: In a chip with many computing cores (think dozens to hundreds on a server processor), parallel programs often need the same shared data — for example, a configuration value or a lock variable — and each core separately asks for it, one after another, causing the same data to travel across the chip's internal wiring network many times. Push Multicast flips the direction: instead of waiting for each core to ask, the last-level cache (the largest, slowest on-chip cache, shared by all cores) predicts which other cores will soon want the same data and proactively sends it to all of them at once in a single 'push.' Smart filters in the network intercept any redundant individual requests that arrive while a push is already in flight, discarding them before they add traffic. A safety valve detects when the proactive pushes are themselves causing congestion and temporarily pauses them.
